content.overview: BNS s. 210 — Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it. BNS restatement of IPC 176. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 176. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 210 is the rule on “Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it”. The section provides that whoever, being legally bound to produce or deliver up any document or electronic record to any public servant, as such, intentionally omits so to produce or deliver up the same,–. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 210 exists so that “Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Summons, proclamations, false information — and the recast suicide-attempt-to-coerce offence.

The provision in detail
210. Whoever, being legally bound to produce or deliver up any document or electronic record to any public servant, as such, intentionally omits so to produce or deliver up the same,–

(a) shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both;

(b) and where the document or electronic record is to be produced or delivered up to a Court with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever, being legally bound to produce or deliver up any document or electronic record to any public servant, as such, intentionally omits so to produce or deliver up the same,–
2. (a) shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both;
3. (b) and where the document or electronic record is to be produced or delivered up to a Court with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, being legally bound to produce a document before a District Court, intentionally omits to produce the same. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 210 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 210 (Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 210 (Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it), Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, being legally bound to produce or deliver up any document or electronic record to any public servant, as such, intentionally omits so to produce or deliver up the same,–
   (2) (a) shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both;
   (3) (b) and where the document or electronic record is to be produced or delivered up to a Court with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 210 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 210 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
